clue.text: International meeting, say, almost completely different …

parts.note: a United Nations convention is one example of an international meeting

indicators.note: almost means the word just short of its last letter is used

parts.note: completely means all

explanation.surface: A diplomat remarks that this international summit was nearly totally unlike the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ALL to AL. The ellipsis runs the clue on into 10 Across, which reuses 'almost completely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of the ordinary, departing from the norm, is different from the usual run.

clue.text: Nearly all of platinum hit is describing wedding

indicators.note: hit suggests the letters are knocked about into a new order
nearly all of means the last letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A wedding song is said to be almost a platinum-selling record.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relating to marriage ceremonies, as in wedding vows or a wedding feast.

clue.text: Just heading off for exam

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: moral means just or righteous

explanation.surface: A student is merely leaving for a test.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, as in a language viva, is called by this name.

clue.text: Request, not popular, to engage one in perversion

indicators.note: to engage means the numeral is taken inside
not means the letters for popular are dropped

parts.note: an invitation is a request to attend
in means popular or fashionable
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An unpopular invitation to take part in something depraved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' tells you to drop the letters for 'popular', and 'to engage' puts the numeral one in the gap that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitiating something corrupts or debases it, so the noun means corruption or distortion.

clue.text: Piece not beginning when nocturne is expected?

indicators.note: not beginning means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a knight is a chess piece

explanation.surface: A musical piece without an opening, at the time a nocturne should play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' looks musical alongside 'nocturne', but it is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturne is a piece evoking the hours of darkness, so that is when one is fitting.

clue.text: I note period nine to engage in mingling

parts.note: a term is a period of time
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone at a party notes it is nearly nine and goes to circulate.
explanation.definitionFit: To blend together or combine is to mingle, so the verb fits.

clue.text: Part of London in North needs a rebuilding

indicators.note: rebuilding means the letters are reconstructed in another order

explanation.surface: A district of north London is in need of redevelopment.
explanation.walkthrough: Neasden is a suburb in north-west London, long a joke in the magazine Private Eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Neasden is a district of the London Borough of Brent.

clue.text: Radio audience mostly staunch aboard ships

indicators.note: aboard means the piece is placed inside the ships

parts.note: liners are large passenger ships

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to staunch a flow is to stem it

explanation.surface: Loyal radio fans are mostly found on board ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staunch' looks like the adjective 'loyal', but it is the verb meaning to stop a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: People tuning into a broadcast hear it rather than watch, so they form its audience.

clue.text: Capture a navy escaping massacre

indicators.note: escaping means those letters get out of the word for massacre

parts.note: carnage is a massacre
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A navy sailor is seized after fleeing a bloodbath.
explanation.definitionFit: To cage an animal is to confine or trap it, so capture is a fair verb.

clue.text: … almost completely excellent, almost first-rate

indicators.note: almost before completely means that word loses its final letter

parts.note: completely means all

indicators.note: almost after excellent again means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: phat is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: Continuing 1 Across, a reviewer hedges: nearly excellent, nearly top quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ALL to AL and the slang PHAT to PHA.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the top grade in some marking schemes, so an alpha piece of work is of the highest class.

clue.text: They try not to meet cost of lump blocking hose

definitions.text: They try not to meet cost

indicators.note: blocking means the lump sits inside, plugging the hose

parts.note: hose is an old word for tights or stockings
a wad is a lump of material

explanation.surface: A plumbing mishap: a chunk of something has clogged the garden hose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hose' suggests a garden pipe, but here it means legwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Misers are reluctant to pay, so they avoid meeting any expense they can.

clue.text: Chap avoiding a man on outskirts of US?

indicators.note: avoiding means those letters are left out of the longer word
on outskirts places the removed letters at the two ends of the word

parts.note: of the United States is American
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone keeps clear of a fellow lurking on the fringes of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: AM comes off the front of AMERICAN and AN off the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric is a man's name, and crosswords often define a first name as a chap.

clue.text: Episode setting standard with launch of telecast

parts.note: par is the standard or norm

indicators.note: launch of means the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A television episode sets the norm when the broadcast begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A serial is broken into instalments, each one a portion of the whole story.

clue.text: Heading away from crossing hilltop?

indicators.note: heading away from means the front letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a bridge is a crossing over a river or road

explanation.surface: A traveller sets off from a crossing point up towards the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long narrow crest of high ground, so loosely the top of a hill.

clue.text: Potential measure about to be taken from rebellion

indicators.note: to be taken from means those letters are removed from the word for rebellion

parts.note: a revolt is a rebellion
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A possible policy, about to be confiscated from rebels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potential' looks like 'possible', but it is electrical potential.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical potential difference is measured in units named after Alessandro Volta.

clue.text: Diva's pure trilling, as observed previously

indicators.note: a diva trilling warbles the notes, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An opera singer's clean trills, as noted earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin tag, meaning see above, refers a reader to an earlier passage.

clue.text: Major technological work? Regularly bring moral code to dismiss study

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the next word is taken
to dismiss means the letters for study are sent away from the word

parts.note: a conscience is one's inner moral code
to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: Advice to bring ethics to bear by abandoning research.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of 'bring' give BIG; CONSCIENCE minus CON leaves SCIENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Large-scale, expensive research projects such as particle colliders are called this as a group.

clue.text: French guy, say, leading soldiers? Several such

indicators.note: leading means the name comes in front of the other piece

parts.note: Serge is a French man's name
soldier ants are a caste of ant, so ants can be soldiers

explanation.surface: A Frenchman in charge of troops; there are several such.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such' points back to 'leading soldiers': NCOs who command a squad.
explanation.definitionFit: These non-commissioned officers lead troops, so several of them are several leaders of soldiers.

clue.text: Telephone staff about a municipal highway?

parts.note: to ring someone is to telephone them

indicators.note: about means the staff goes round the a

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Phone the council workers about a town road.
explanation.definitionFit: A road circling a town to divert traffic from its centre is a bypass of this kind.

clue.text: Journal covering legal case (except the start)? Lots of words here

indicators.note: covering means the journal wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a diary is a journal

indicators.note: except the start means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: an action is a legal case or lawsuit

explanation.surface: A notebook records a lawsuit, missing its beginning, and holds many words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' tells you the journal wraps round the shortened lawsuit; 'except the start' removes only the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lexicon lists a language's vocabulary, so it is a book holding a great many words.

clue.text: Empress, last character to board vehicle in area

indicators.note: to board means the letter gets inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
Z is the final letter of the alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: An empress is the final figure to step into the carriage locally.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a Russian emperor, holding the rank of empress.

clue.text: Tends to drop a glass

indicators.note: to drop means the a is let fall out of the word

parts.note: leans means tends or inclines

explanation.surface: Someone is inclined to let a drinking glass slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A lens is a shaped piece of glass, as in spectacles or a camera.

clue.text: Single shot by Henry from European country

indicators.note: shot means wrecked, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Someone from a European nation scores a single hit off a man called Henry.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective naming people or things from England, a European country.

clue.text: Working hard to erase six words of vulgar tendencies?

indicators.note: to erase means the Roman numeral is wiped out of the word

parts.note: slaving is working hard
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone toils to delete half a dozen rude words.
explanation.walkthrough: Tendencies hints at slang being casual, informal speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal, often coarse vocabulary outside standard usage is called by this name.

clue.text: Small garden area, fitted at an angle

parts.note: Kew, in west London, is home to the Royal Botanic Gardens

explanation.surface: A little garden plot has been laid out on the slant.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW is the London district famous for the Royal Botanic Gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Something askew is slanted, set obliquely rather than straight.

clue.text: One brought in revolutionary copies of old photographs?

indicators.note: brought in means the numeral is put inside
revolutionary means the word is turned right round

parts.note: apes means copies or imitates
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A figure brought in to make revolutionary reproductions of vintage pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Early photographic prints were toned a reddish brown, the colour this word names.

clue.text: Threatening limits to using library

indicators.note: limits to means the first and last letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: Restrictions on library use are menacing.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugly mood or situation is menacing, likely to turn violent.

clue.text: Yellow jersey ultimately very good, worn by first in line

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of jersey
worn by here means the letter is enclosed by the other piece

parts.note: OK means all right, good

indicators.note: first in means the opening letter of line

explanation.surface: Cycling: the yellow jersey is finally doing very well, worn by the race leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow centre of an egg is called by this name.

clue.text: What may be seen in Amritsar (India)?

definitions.text: What may be seen in Amritsar (India)?

indicators.note: what may be seen in means the letters lie inside the following words

explanation.surface: A question about what a visitor might see in the Indian city of Amritsar.
explanation.definitionFit: Women in India commonly wear this draped garment, so one may be seen in Amritsar.

clue.text: Post Office is trading, welcoming new source of malicious mail

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: welcoming means the shop takes the other letter inside

parts.note: a shop that is open is trading

explanation.surface: The Post Office is open for business and accepts a fresh supply of hate mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers of anonymous spiteful letters are known by this phrase.

clue.text: Sign left for second satellite

indicators.note: left for second means one letter replaces the other

parts.note: Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A signal leaves for a second orbiting body.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is one of the moons of Uranus, a natural satellite.

clue.text: Pop film always presented in unusually high standard

indicators.note: presented in means the word for always goes inside the rearranged letters
unusually means the letters are set out in an odd new order

parts.note: ay is a poetic or dialect word for always

explanation.surface: An exceptionally good pop film, consistently so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges HIGH STANDARD, with AY placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles starred in this 1964 film, named after one of their songs.
